Beijing: reproduce the saved traffic-map figures

This tutorial reproduces the data layers in the existing Beijing traffic visualization using bdynets. The standalone dataset was extracted losslessly from the HTML. It contains 288 five-minute frames, matched road polylines and rounded relative-load values. It is the actual repository visualization dataset, not a synthetic example. Raw trajectory files are not required. No model is fitted and no JavaScript or network request runs.

Read and inspect the standalone saved data

Install bdynets from the repository package subdirectory and install jsonlite if needed. Rendering this tutorial additionally requires rmarkdown and knitr.

library(bdynets)
snapshot <- read_traffic_data(params$snapshot)
data.frame(edges=length(snapshot$ids), frames=length(snapshot$bins),
           minutes_per_frame=snapshot$bin_minutes)
##   edges frames minutes_per_frame
## 1 11742    288                 5

The source metric is x_ijt / estimated capacity; it is relative load, not an observed accident count or a probability. Values are preserved at the HTML’s saved precision. An edge absent from a frame follows the original viewer’s zero convention. That convention belongs to this visualization export and must not be generalized to missing observations in other datasets.

Reproduce the three views

Frame 107 is 08:50–08:55 (R indexing starts at one). It has the highest saved mean relative load and highest saved count of high-load edges. This is a transparent descriptive selection, not evidence about a model’s performance. The shared package workflow below is also called by run.R.

frames <- traffic_figures(params$snapshot, "beijing", time_index=107L)

The first map uses the source’s 0%, 20%, 40%, 60% and 80%+ classes. Gray roads have zero displayed load. The second map uses red for increases and blue for decreases relative to the preceding five-minute frame; width represents change magnitude. The third shows consecutive time above the viewer’s 80% threshold, using the saved duration records, with bins converted to minutes.

Matched road polylines and Web Mercator projection are retained. These are static data-layer reproductions: remote OpenStreetMap tiles, place labels and browser controls are omitted. Line widths are adapted to a static graphics device. The figures are therefore not pixel-identical screenshots.

Select another frame or export publication assets

frame <- traffic_frame(snapshot, time_index=97L, mode="current")
plot(frame) # 08:00–08:05
traffic_figures(params$snapshot, "beijing", time_index=97L,
                output_dir="output/beijing-0800")

The export writes PDF and PNG figures, a source-file MD5/selection record and session information. Existing named outputs are refused. To reuse these data for inference, obtain the underlying counts and exposure: rounded ratios are not valid substitutes for count responses.
